walkthroughs.body_html: Antony Gormley's Angel of the North was installed near Gateshead in 1998. It stands 20 m tall with a 54 m wingspan, made of weathering steel. Built on a former colliery site, it honours coal-mining history.
Many of Gormley's works begin as body casts of himself, then translate that human-scale form into iron, steel or cast figures. The result is intimate — a single body — and yet, blown up, monumental.

Public sculpture has no ticket — it meets audiences who may not visit galleries. Choices of scale, material durability, weather resistance and even sight from a passing motorway all become part of the brief.
